questions.prompt: Which statement gives the core rule for “Watchdogs, debugging, and production patterns”?
options: The scheduler runs tasks; `vTaskDelay` lets other work use the CPU.
A watchdog triggers recovery but does not identify the root cause; retain logs, measurements, and fault records.
Each task consumes stack; priority affects scheduler choices.
Start with a simple `loop()`; add tasks only for independent work with distinct timing needs.
questions.answer: A watchdog triggers recovery but does not identify the root cause; retain logs, measurements, and fault records.
questions.explanation:
A watchdog triggers recovery but does not identify the root cause; retain logs, measurements, and fault records.
Why: A watchdog restarts a system when expected progress stops; use it as a health contract, not as a blind reset. Tasks should report progress only after useful work, and logs or core dumps should help diagnose blocking and deadlocks. Production firmware also needs bounded queues, timeouts, retry/backoff, stack measurements, and a recovery plan.

`esp_task_wdt_*` are Espressif ESP-IDF APIs exposed by some Arduino-ESP32 core versions, not portable Arduino APIs. For another board, implement an appropriate health/timeout strategy and verify the selected core's support.

An infinite task should block or wait periodically so it does not monopolize the CPU.
